notes: The DARK ANCHOR. Every landscape reference leans on one: cliffs-tohad.jpg's near hedges, grasslands.jpg's conifer masses, water-lagoon.webp's palm shade. Without something authored genuinely dark the frame has no bottom to its value range — measured p05 of HSV value sat at 0.62 against 0.48 in the references — and 'lifted shadows' degenerates into 'no darks at all'. So this def is deliberately 2.5 stops under the meadow it sits on, and it stays chromatic (deep emerald, not black) the way ART_BIBLE 2 requires. gradientBase/gradientHeight are OBJECT space and this geometry is unit-sized: metre-scale values here saturate the sweep to a constant and switch the vertical gradient off entirely, which is how every instanced asset in the greybox lost it. Saturation corrected: lit must sit BELOW shadow in chroma (measured -0.15 across references); the earlier ART_BIBLE rule had this inverted. Brush overlay reduced 0.9 -> 0.18: the painterly direction is abandoned (ART_BIBLE 1) and this was still running at full strength, which is the camouflage mottle on terrain. PAINTERLY OVERLAY REMOVED IN THE DATA, all five knobs, not just the obvious one. `brushStrength` was already 0 on this def and the surface still rendered as leopard print, because `brushHue` (an albedo hue rotation), `detailStrength` (a normal perturbation), `regionStep` (a coarse mass mask) and `reliefShade` (an AMBIENT mottle) are all read independently of it in painterly.ts. Measured on one flat rock facet, a 20x20 window ran luma sd 0.106-0.148 against 0.015-0.042 for a facet in refs/genshin/grasslands.jpg — 3.5-10x. The whole point of a plane-cut solid is that a facet is exactly planar so the 3-stop ramp reads it as ONE flat value, and this was destroying that on every asset in the library. ART_BIBLE 1: "No brush-stroke overlay on terrain. Surfaces are clean." SUPERSEDED FOR SCATTER BY `leaf`. Every asset in src/assets now names `leaf` instead of `bush`, because src/world/surfaceGrade.ts's GRADE table has an entry for `bush` and `graded()` applies it AFTER the def and after any per-def override — so a corrected value authored here changes the Forge and leaves the game pixel where it was. This def is now the TERRAIN's, which is the world team's to grade; see assets/defs/surfaces/leaf.json for the measured scatter grade. If the GRADE entry for `bush` is ever retired, the two can be merged back.
